# Original HUC05–07 daily discharge source

Operation: A74F-USGS-DISCHARGE-20261013. This package follows A73C's original regional calibration acquisition request and preserves eight complete USGS response bodies (926,648 bytes), their query URLs, retrieval stamps and SHA256 identities.

## Usable measurements

The period-of-record selection contains thirteen USGS daily-mean discharge series under source HUC8 codes 03060105, 03060106 and 03060107. It selects original `data_type_cd=dv`, `parm_cd=00060`, `stat_cd=00003`, with catalogue dates overlapping 2020-01-01 through 2025-12-31. The response includes other parameters for qualifying sites; the selected thirteen original `ts_id` values bind the actual discharge records.

The six complete annual responses contain 26,242 original records and 26,241 numeric values. The original `Rat` value at station 02196690 on 2024-09-24 remains nonnumeric with its provisional `P` qualifier. There are 654 estimated numeric values and 13 provisional numeric values; the provisional nonnumeric record makes 14 provisional source records. All source flags remain present in the daily CSV. Seven gauges contain all 2,192 numeric calendar days. Other gauges retain their original shorter records or gaps.

## Files and direct use

`source-manifest.json` retains every request and source identity, the complete thirteen selected catalogue rows, original datum information and the retained 217-HUC context. `original/` contains the unchanged expanded site inventory, full period-of-record catalogue and six annual daily source responses. `derived/daily-discharge.csv` contains all 26,242 records with original site, time-series identity, reported text, parsed numeric cfs value when present, qualifiers, original source path and source line. `derived/station-year-coverage.csv` gives 78 station/year summaries; the companion JSON also retains exact missing-date and nonnumeric-date ranges.

Values are daily means in cubic feet per second. Means and ranges in the coverage summaries describe available numeric days only. The calendar denominator includes every day in the named year, including leap days. The summary leaves absent days explicit and counts estimated, approved and provisional observations separately. Use the original qualifiers when selecting data for a particular scientific analysis.

## Original spatial join

The expanded site records expose publisher HUC8 and NAD83 coordinates. The local retained original 217-polygon domain determines exact station inclusion in the model, reporting or utility geography. Its source ID is `upstate-wbd-upstream-domain-20261012`; original compressed body SHA256 `6f49c2f1dc10709d7957e38e92642a1de4cda44e67e4d70a8bc2ff51388e6af9`. The maintained source/water_context/20261013/full-domain-water-context.json carries 217 selected HUC12 identities, including 49 under the three queried HUC8 parents. The source manifest includes those 49 identities and exact original context Git blob `80e9447b1e49c2de479fd24a6a38f766932a903b`. Transform original station coordinates from their declared NAD83 datum into the original domain CRS using the native geometry pipeline, then perform the exact point/polygon join. Preserve boundary cases explicitly.

A gauge's monitoring point and complete contributing catchment are separate spatial selections. The maintained calibration workflow binds the original upstream catchment and its source period to any modeled comparison. The dataset supplies discharge observations for that workflow and supports original-date concentration/flow matching.

## Reproduce the derivation offline

Use Node's standard library:

```sh
node derive-discharge.mjs /absolute/path/to/source-packet /absolute/path/to/output
```

The included module hashes all eight originals before parsing. It understands repeated RDB blocks, checks daily source identity and date, selects exact 00060/00003 columns, retains original `ts_id` and qualifiers, rejects duplicate series/date rows, and reproduces the full CSV plus 78 station/year coverage records. The complete published derivation was run against all eight actual original responses in the available JavaScript runtime; its daily CSV and coverage CSV reproduce the retained outputs byte for byte. All 26,242 source rows retain original paths/line numbers.

# Additional regional discharge calibration context

This is the six-year extension of the maintained Upper Savannah observed hydrology workflow. It uses A74F's eight original USGS responses for thirteen native daily-mean discharge series in HUC8 groups 03060105, 03060106 and 03060107. The original 16-gauge edition remains available with its original source identities. The two inventories select 29 distinct gauges; their periods, native time-series IDs and source geometry remain separate.

## What the retained measurements add

The six original annual responses contain 26,242 source records, of which 26,241 are numeric. The source includes 654 estimated numeric values and 13 provisional numeric values. Horse Creek station02196690 retains the nonnumeric text `Rat` with provisional qualifier `P` on2024-09-24. There are 61 complete calendar-years and all61 contain approved numeric values on every date. The additional context has 78 annual rows, 936 monthly rows and 13 rows for the original lake-study window2023-04-05 through2023-10-17.

The following annual comparison uses each station's complete approved 2023 mean against the median of its other complete approved calendar-year means from 2020–2025. Estimated values already approved by USGS remain included and are counted explicitly. The reference-year count matters: a two-year median and a five-year median describe different retained support.

Kiokee Creek's2023 mean is about59.2% above the median of its five other complete years, while Little River is about11.7% below its corresponding median. Stevens Creek is about11.4% above. Savannah River at Augusta and Burtons Ferry are within roughly0.6% of their respective reference medians. These station-specific differences support explicit period and catchment selection in the original NDR/SDR workflow.

Augusta Canal has327 numeric dates in2023 and no reported drainage area in the original station inventory. Its available-day mean is retained, while annual volume, annual runoff and the complete-year comparison ratio remain unavailable. Savannah River near Waynesboro has344 numeric dates in2023; its observed-day volume remains separate from a full-year total. The one available complete reference year at that station does not supply a long-term climatology.

## Numerical and source conventions

The existing hydrology conventions are preserved: discharge parameter00060, daily-mean statistic00003, native TS_ID, calendar dates, cubic feet per second,0.028316846592 m³/s per cfs and86,400 seconds per nominal reporting day. Original decimal spellings are summed using exact integers before floating-point conversion. Percentiles interpolate at(n−1)p on sorted valid daily values. The low-flow fifth percentile is the fifth percentile of discharge, not a95% exceedance label.

Observed-period volumes sum only numeric original days. Full-period volume and runoff are populated only when every expected calendar date has a numeric daily mean. Missing dates and source nonnumeric values have separate counts and ranges. Approved, estimated, provisional and revised flags are counted independently; estimated approved values remain approved. Approved-only observed volume is retained alongside all-numeric observed volume.

Runoff divides the observed volume by the original reported drainage area in square miles, converted using2,589,988.110336 m² per square mile. That quantity describes the gauge's source drainage area. It is not the runoff of a model domain merely because the monitoring point lies inside it. Canal discharge and nested river gauges remain separate series; adding their volumes would double count routed water.

## Geographic use in the retained model

The source site inventory supplies NAD83 coordinates and HUC8 codes. The regional domain contains49 selected HUC12 polygons under these three parents:18 in03060105,8 in03060106 and23 in03060107. `source-manifest.json` retains the exact49 identifiers and original217-HUC domain identity. `derived/calibration_stations_nad83.geojson` retains all13 native monitoring points, source coordinate metadata and the original inventory hash.

The original domain pipeline must transform these NAD83 points into the retained domain CRS and distinguish interior, boundary and outside results. A monitoring-point join and the full contributing-basin overlap answer different questions. The original NLDI basin capture is being joined through its source owner; use its exact point/COMID/reach/measure and full upstream polygon alongside the selected model catchment. Station HUC8 alone does not supply that relation.

For native NDR comparisons, carry the correct catchment area, period and runoff-proxy normalization from the existing calibration guide. Annual discharge helps interpret hydrologic context; nutrient and sediment calibration still uses matching constituent measurements and model export quantities. The retained exact same-outlet WQP nutrient query for USGS02186702 over2020–2025 returned a63-column header with zero result rows. That query result remains in the adjacent source/calibration-coverage/20261013 capture with its exact site/date/category selection.

## Source intake and reproduction

Import `model-sources.json` through the existing Sources intake. It provides the original13 monitoring points, full daily source join, comparable annual/monthly/study-window summaries and2023 reference context. The documentation entry carries every original response, native source manifest, original derivation, current computation and complete output inventory as companions.

Reproduce the added six outputs with Node's standard library:

```sh
node rebuild_calibration.mjs --output-dir /absolute/path/to/rebuilt-context
```

The command verifies the source manifest, all eight original bodies and both calculation modules. It executes the retained original `derive()` reader, preserves original paths and line numbers, and verifies every generated output against `calibration-inputs.json` before writing. The original daily CSV and source coverage products remain unchanged.

Original query URLs, source retrieval stamps, native period-of-record selection and body hashes are in `source-manifest.json`. The daily CSV retains source path and line for every original record. The numerical conventions match `observations/observed_hydrology_20261013/hydrology_core.mjs`; the current model application guidance remains in its `CALIBRATION_CONTEXT.md`.

Annual and monthly tables also retain the volume fraction carried by source-estimated daily values and the fraction carried by days strictly above that period's own daily-flow95th percentile. These are observed-date volume partitions. They help assess the relative weight of qualified or high-flow observations without turning either fraction into a confidence interval.

# Original daily-flow gauges and upstream catchment support

This source edition binds thirteen original USGS daily-discharge series to their original NLDI station features and upstream NHDPlusV2 catchment geometries. It contains 26 unchanged publisher responses (831,742 bytes), complete request URLs and SHA256 identities, exact source station/series bindings, portable GeoJSON views, and an offline derivation module.

The source accompanies the complete 2020–2025 discharge edition merged in [PR3038](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/3038). The adjacent daily source supplies 26,242 records and 78 station-year coverage summaries. Use the original qualifiers and periods when selecting observations.

## Spatial meaning

Every basin query explicitly sets `simplified=false` and `splitCatchment=false`. The original response aggregates complete upstream catchments, including the entire local catchment associated with the station's source COMID. All original polygon components, holes, vertices and coordinate values remain intact in the derived collection. Native area calculations should transform this source geometry into the selected projected CRS.

The registered gauge location, its measure along a source reach, the whole upstream catchment support and an exact gauge-split support are distinct source selections. The regional context can use the supplied whole-catchment support directly. The maintained annual-load calibration workflow binds the catchment support declared by its original estimator and observation selection. A precise gauge-split response, when received, travels as a separate edition with `splitCatchment=true`.

NLDI geometry uses the publisher's GeoJSON longitude/latitude coordinates. The original NWIS station inventory separately declares each decimal-coordinate datum; those fields are retained verbatim. Original NLDI and NWIS point values remain separate. The module performs no local coordinate transformation or simplification.

## Files

- `original/<site>.feature.json`: unchanged original NLDI station response, including COMID, reach code, measure and mainstem reference.
- `original/<site>.whole-basin.geojson`: unchanged original full upstream whole-catchment response.
- `capture-manifest.json`: original request parameters, full body identities, exact selected NWIS catalog/inventory rows and original 217-HUC source binding.
- `derived/stations.geojson`: thirteen original point geometries with source and daily-series bindings.
- `derived/upstream-whole-catchments.geojson`: thirteen original basin geometries with a stable `basin_id` and the same station bindings.
- `derived/station-basin-bindings.csv` and `.json`: thirteen full identity records, source periods, datum information, original paths/hashes, geometry structure counts and bounds.
- `model-sources.json`: three complete native source entries, including all original companions and reproducible derivation.
- `derive-basins.mjs`: standard-library Node module that verifies all original hashes and rebuilds the four derived files.

The stable station ID is `USGS-<site_no>`. The whole-catchment ID is `nldi-nwissite-USGS-<site_no>-whole`. Use `basin_id` as the vector identity field for this geometry edition. Original daily series identity remains `ts_id`; a station's ID and its series ID are separate fields.

## Import into the existing Workspace

From the current application root:

```sh
"$PYTHON" -B -m model.cli --workspace "$WORKSPACE" source-import source/hydrology-huc05-07-20261013/nldi/model-sources.json
```

This imports the original files and all companions through the maintained `Workspace.import_sources` API. Native source IDs are:

- `nldi-daily-flow-gauge-locations-20261013`
- `nldi-daily-flow-whole-catchments-20261013`
- `nldi-daily-flow-station-basin-bindings-20261013`

The regional support desk reuses the existing station-geography point/polygon engine and original watershed/network source. A73C / OBS12 / AE11 retain the discharge/concentration and annual-estimator intake; the maintained calibration workflow consumes the resulting original observation and catchment selection.

## Reproduce the derived source views

```sh
node derive-basins.mjs /absolute/path/to/nldi /absolute/path/to/rebuilt
```

The module verifies every original byte count and SHA256, checks exact source station IDs and query choices, retains geometry coordinates, and writes four deterministic outputs. It reuses identical output files and refuses to replace a different edition. The published derivation was executed over all 26 original responses in the available JavaScript runtime.
